'''Rose Pauline Peltesohn''' ({{Langx|he|רוז פאולין פלטסון}}; 16 May 1913 – 21 March 1998) was an Israeli mathematician of German origin.

==Life==
Rose Peltesohn was the daughter of the physician Ludwig Peltesohn (1882–1937) and of Cilly Caro.<ref>Peltesohn (1936), p.20; in contrast, [[Renate Tobies]]' short biography uses "Zili"</ref> After graduation (Abitur) in March 1931 she studied mathematics and physics at the [[Humboldt-Universität Berlin|University of Berlin]] and got her Ph.D. in Mathematics at 1936 with  [[Issai Schur]]<ref>Rose Peltesohn, [http://www.sweet-art.co.il/Rose_peltesohn/Rose_Peltesohn-Das%20Turnierproblem_fur_Spiele_zu_je_dreien.pdf Das Turnierproblem für Spiele zu je dreien], 1936, p. 2, 20</ref> as supervisor (''Das Turnierproblem für Spiele zu je dreien'', The tournament problem for three person games). Her dissertation was valued ''opus valde laudabile''<sup>([[:de:Dissertation#Bewertungsstufen einer Dissertation|de]])</sup>. Being Jewish she emigrated through Italy to Palestine, arriving 1938.<ref name="Siegmund-Schultze2009">{{cite book|author=Reinhard Siegmund-Schultze|title=Mathematicians Fleeing from Nazi Germany: Individual Fates and Global Impact|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=rdDvIYYTtrgC&pg=PA19|accessdate=31 October 2018|date=6 July 2009|publisher=Princeton University Press|isbn=978-1-4008-3140-1|pages=19, 128, 353}}</ref> Between the years 1939–1942 she worked in a bank and later as a lawyer's secretary and translator in Tel Aviv. She married her cousin Gerhard Peltesohn, a lawyer (1909–1965), and they had two daughters, Ruth (born 1940) and Judith (born 1943).

==Solution of Heffter's Difference Problems==
Peltesohn solved the Difference Problems of {{ill|Lothar Heffter|de}} (1896) in combinatorics in 1939.<ref>{{cite journal| author=Rose Peltesohn |title=Eine Lösung der beiden Heffterschen Differenzenprobleme |journal=Compositio Mathematica| volume=6 |year=1939 |pages=251–257 |url=http://archive.numdam.org/article/CM_1939__6__251_0.pdf}}</ref> A Difference Triple (''a'',&nbsp;''b'',&nbsp;''c'') is defined as three different elements from the set <math>1, 2,\dots, v-1</math>, whose sum <math>\bmod v</math> equals zero (<math>a+b+c=0 \bmod v</math>) or for which one element <math>\bmod v</math> equals the sum of the other two (<math>a+b=c \bmod v</math>).
*First Difference Problem of Heffter: Let <math>v=6 m+1</math>. Is there a partition of the set <math>1, 2,\ldots, 3m</math> in difference triples?
*Second Difference Problem of Heffter: Let <math> v=6m+3</math>. Is there a partition of the set <math>1,2,\ldots,2m, 2m+2,\ldots, 3m+1</math> in difference triples ?

Following Peltesohn, such a partition exists with the exception of the case&nbsp;''v''&nbsp;=&nbsp;9.

An example of the partition for <math>v=13</math> is: <math>(1,3,4)</math> (with <math>1+3=4 \bmod 13</math>) and <math>(2,5,6)</math> (with <math>2+5+6=13=0 \bmod 13</math>).

The solution of the Difference Problem of Heffter also gives a construction of cyclic [[Steiner system#Steiner triple systems|Steiner triple systems]].
